================
File: gh-md-toc
================
  1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
  2: 
  3: #
  4: # Steps:
  5: #
  6: #  1. Download corresponding html file for some README.md:
  7: #       curl -s $1
  8: #
  9: #  2. Discard rows where no substring 'user-content-' (github's markup):
 10: #       awk '/user-content-/ { ...
 11: #
 12: #  3.1 Get last number in each row like ' ... </span></a>sitemap.js</h1'.
 13: #      It's a level of the current header:
 14: #       substr($0, length($0), 1)
 15: #
 16: #  3.2 Get level from 3.1 and insert corresponding number of spaces before '*':
 17: #       sprintf("%*s", substr($0, length($0), 1)*2, " ")
 18: #
 19: #  4. Find head's text and insert it inside "* [ ... ]":
 20: #       substr($0, match($0, /a>.*<\/h/)+2, RLENGTH-5)
 21: #
 22: #  5. Find anchor and insert it inside "(...)":
 23: #       substr($0, match($0, "href=\"[^\"]+?\" ")+6, RLENGTH-8)
 24: #
 25: 
 26: gh_toc_version="0.4.7"
 27: 
 28: gh_user_agent="gh-md-toc v$gh_toc_version"
 29: 
 30: #
 31: # Download rendered into html README.md by its url.
 32: #
 33: #
 34: gh_toc_load() {
 35:     local gh_url=$1
 36: 
 37:     if type curl &>/dev/null; then
 38:         curl --user-agent "$gh_user_agent" -s "$gh_url"
 39:     elif type wget &>/dev/null; then
 40:         wget --user-agent="$gh_user_agent" -qO- "$gh_url"
 41:     else
 42:         echo "Please, install 'curl' or 'wget' and try again."
 43:         exit 1
 44:     fi
 45: }
 46: 
 47: #
 48: # Converts local md file into html by GitHub
 49: #
 50: # ➥ curl -X POST --data '{"text": "Hello world github/linguist#1 **cool**, and #1!"}' https://api.github.com/markdown
 51: # <p>Hello world github/linguist#1 <strong>cool</strong>, and #1!</p>'"
 52: gh_toc_md2html() {
 53:     local gh_file_md=$1
 54:     curl -s --user-agent "$gh_user_agent" \
 55:         --data-binary @"$gh_file_md" -H "Content-Type:text/plain" \
 56:         https://api.github.com/markdown/raw
 57: }
 58: 
 59: #
 60: # Is passed string url
 61: #
 62: gh_is_url() {
 63:     if [[ $1 == https* || $1 == http* ]]; then
 64:         echo "yes"
 65:     else
 66:         echo "no"
 67:     fi
 68: }
 69: 
 70: #
 71: # TOC generator
 72: #
 73: gh_toc(){
 74:     local gh_src=$1
 75:     local gh_src_copy=$1
 76:     local gh_ttl_docs=$2
 77: 
 78:     if [ "$gh_src" = "" ]; then
 79:         echo "Please, enter URL or local path for a README.md"
 80:         exit 1
 81:     fi
 82: 
 83: 
 84:     # Show "TOC" string only if working with one document
 85:     if [ "$gh_ttl_docs" = "1" ]; then
 86: 
 87:         echo "Table of Contents"
 88:         echo "================="
 89:         echo ""
 90:         gh_src_copy=""
 91: 
 92:     fi
 93: 
 94:     if [ "$(gh_is_url "$gh_src")" == "yes" ]; then
 95:         gh_toc_load "$gh_src" | gh_toc_grab "$gh_src_copy"
 96:     else
 97:         gh_toc_md2html "$gh_src" | gh_toc_grab "$gh_src_copy"
 98:     fi
 99: }
100: 
101: #
102: # Grabber of the TOC from rendered html
103: #
104: # $1 — a source url of document.
105: # It's need if TOC is generated for multiple documents.
106: #
107: gh_toc_grab() {
108: 	# if closed <h[1-6]> is on the new line, then move it on the prev line
109: 	# for example:
110: 	# 	was: The command <code>foo1</code>
111: 	# 		 </h1>
112: 	# 	became: The command <code>foo1</code></h1>
113:     sed -e ':a' -e 'N' -e '$!ba' -e 's/\n<\/h/<\/h/g' |
114:     # find strings that corresponds to template
115:     grep -E -o '<a\s*id="user-content-[^"]*".*</h[1-6]' |
116:     # remove code tags
117:     sed 's/<code>//' | sed 's/<\/code>//' |
118:     # now all rows are like:
119:     #   <a id="user-content-..." href="..."><span ...></span></a> ... </h1
120:     # format result line
121:     #   * $0 — whole string
122:     echo -e "$(awk -v "gh_url=$1" '{
123:     print sprintf("%*s", substr($0, length($0), 1)*3, " ") "* [" substr($0, match($0, /a>.*<\/h/)+2, RLENGTH-5)"](" gh_url substr($0, match($0, "href=\"[^\"]+?\" ")+6, RLENGTH-8) ")"}' | sed 'y/+/ /; s/%/\\x/g')"
124: }
125: 
126: #
127: # Returns filename only from full path or url
128: #
129: gh_toc_get_filename() {
130:     echo "${1##*/}"
131: }
132: 
133: #
134: # Options hendlers
135: #
136: gh_toc_app() {
137:     local app_name="gh-md-toc"
138: 
139:     if [ "$1" = '--help' ] || [ $# -eq 0 ] ; then
140:         echo "GitHub TOC generator ($app_name): $gh_toc_version"
141:         echo ""
142:         echo "Usage:"
143:         echo "  $app_name src [src]     Create TOC for a README file (url or local path)"
144:         echo "  $app_name -             Create TOC for markdown from STDIN"
145:         echo "  $app_name --help        Show help"
146:         echo "  $app_name --version     Show version"
147:         return
148:     fi
149: 
150:     if [ "$1" = '--version' ]; then
151:         echo "$gh_toc_version"
152:         return
153:     fi
154: 
155:     if [ "$1" = "-" ]; then
156:         if [ -z "$TMPDIR" ]; then
157:             TMPDIR="/tmp"
158:         elif [ -n "$TMPDIR" -a ! -d "$TMPDIR" ]; then
159:             mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
160:         fi
161:         local gh_tmp_md
162:         gh_tmp_md=$(mktemp $TMPDIR/tmp.XXXXXX)
163:         while read input; do
164:             echo "$input" >> "$gh_tmp_md"
165:         done
166:         gh_toc_md2html "$gh_tmp_md" | gh_toc_grab ""
167:         return
168:     fi
169: 
170:     for md in "$@"
171:     do
172:         echo ""
173:         gh_toc "$md" "$#"
174:     done
175: 
176:     echo ""
177:     echo "Created by [gh-md-toc](https://github.com/ekalinin/github-markdown-toc)"
178: }
179: 
180: #
181: # Entry point
182: #
183: gh_toc_app "$@"

File: monolithic/mvnw

  1: #!/bin/sh
  2: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3: # Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one
  4: # or more contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file
  5: # distributed with this work for additional information
  6: # regarding copyright ownership.  The ASF licenses this file
  7: # to you under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the
  8: # "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance
  9: # with the License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
 10: #
 11: #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 12: #
 13: # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
 14: # software distributed under the License is distributed on an
 15: # "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY
 16: # KIND, either express or implied.  See the License for the
 17: # specific language governing permissions and limitations
 18: # under the License.
 19: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 20: 
 21: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 22: # Maven2 Start Up Batch script
 23: #
 24: # Required ENV vars:
 25: # ------------------
 26: #   JAVA_HOME - location of a JDK home dir
 27: #
 28: # Optional ENV vars
 29: # -----------------
 30: #   M2_HOME - location of maven2's installed home dir
 31: #   MAVEN_OPTS - parameters passed to the Java VM when running Maven
 32: #     e.g. to debug Maven itself, use
 33: #       set MAVEN_OPTS=-Xdebug -Xrunjdwp:transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=8000
 34: #   MAVEN_SKIP_RC - flag to disable loading of mavenrc files
 35: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36: 
 37: if [ -z "$MAVEN_SKIP_RC" ] ; then
 38: 
 39:   if [ -f /etc/mavenrc ] ; then
 40:     . /etc/mavenrc
 41:   fi
 42: 
 43:   if [ -f "$HOME/.mavenrc" ] ; then
 44:     . "$HOME/.mavenrc"
 45:   fi
 46: 
 47: fi
 48: 
 49: # OS specific support.  $var _must_ be set to either true or false.
 50: cygwin=false;
 51: darwin=false;
 52: mingw=false
 53: case "`uname`" in
 54:   CYGWIN*) cygwin=true ;;
 55:   MINGW*) mingw=true;;
 56:   Darwin*) darwin=true
 57:            #
 58:            # Look for the Apple JDKs first to preserve the existing behaviour, and then look
 59:            # for the new JDKs provided by Oracle.
 60:            #
 61:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L /System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/CurrentJDK ] ; then
 62:              #
 63:              # Apple JDKs
 64:              #
 65:              export JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/CurrentJDK/Home
 66:            fi
 67: 
 68:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L /System/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK ] ; then
 69:              #
 70:              # Apple JDKs
 71:              #
 72:              export JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK/Contents/Home
 73:            fi
 74: 
 75:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L "/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK" ] ; then
 76:              #
 77:              # Oracle JDKs
 78:              #
 79:              export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK/Contents/Home
 80:            fi
 81: 
 82:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -x "/usr/libexec/java_home" ]; then
 83:              #
 84:              # Apple JDKs
 85:              #
 86:              export JAVA_HOME=`/usr/libexec/java_home`
 87:            fi
 88:            ;;
 89: esac
 90: 
 91: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
 92:   if [ -r /etc/gentoo-release ] ; then
 93:     JAVA_HOME=`java-config --jre-home`
 94:   fi
 95: fi
 96: 
 97: if [ -z "$M2_HOME" ] ; then
 98:   ## resolve links - $0 may be a link to maven's home
 99:   PRG="$0"
100: 
101:   # need this for relative symlinks
102:   while [ -h "$PRG" ] ; do
103:     ls=`ls -ld "$PRG"`
104:     link=`expr "$ls" : '.*-> \(.*\)$'`
105:     if expr "$link" : '/.*' > /dev/null; then
106:       PRG="$link"
107:     else
108:       PRG="`dirname "$PRG"`/$link"
109:     fi
110:   done
111: 
112:   saveddir=`pwd`
113: 
114:   M2_HOME=`dirname "$PRG"`/..
115: 
116:   # make it fully qualified
117:   M2_HOME=`cd "$M2_HOME" && pwd`
118: 
119:   cd "$saveddir"
120:   # echo Using m2 at $M2_HOME
121: fi
122: 
123: # For Cygwin, ensure paths are in UNIX format before anything is touched
124: if $cygwin ; then
125:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
126:     M2_HOME=`cygpath --unix "$M2_HOME"`
127:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
128:     JAVA_HOME=`cygpath --unix "$JAVA_HOME"`
129:   [ -n "$CLASSPATH" ] &&
130:     CLASSPATH=`cygpath --path --unix "$CLASSPATH"`
131: fi
132: 
133: # For Migwn, ensure paths are in UNIX format before anything is touched
134: if $mingw ; then
135:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
136:     M2_HOME="`(cd "$M2_HOME"; pwd)`"
137:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
138:     JAVA_HOME="`(cd "$JAVA_HOME"; pwd)`"
139:   # TODO classpath?
140: fi
141: 
142: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ]; then
143:   javaExecutable="`which javac`"
144:   if [ -n "$javaExecutable" ] && ! [ "`expr \"$javaExecutable\" : '\([^ ]*\)'`" = "no" ]; then
145:     # readlink(1) is not available as standard on Solaris 10.
146:     readLink=`which readlink`
147:     if [ ! `expr "$readLink" : '\([^ ]*\)'` = "no" ]; then
148:       if $darwin ; then
149:         javaHome="`dirname \"$javaExecutable\"`"
150:         javaExecutable="`cd \"$javaHome\" && pwd -P`/javac"
151:       else
152:         javaExecutable="`readlink -f \"$javaExecutable\"`"
153:       fi
154:       javaHome="`dirname \"$javaExecutable\"`"
155:       javaHome=`expr "$javaHome" : '\(.*\)/bin'`
156:       JAVA_HOME="$javaHome"
157:       export JAVA_HOME
158:     fi
159:   fi
160: fi
161: 
162: if [ -z "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
163:   if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME"  ] ; then
164:     if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
165:       # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
166:       JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java"
167:     else
168:       JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"
169:     fi
170:   else
171:     JAVACMD="`which java`"
172:   fi
173: fi
174: 
175: if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
176:   echo "Error: JAVA_HOME is not defined correctly." >&2
177:   echo "  We cannot execute $JAVACMD" >&2
178:   exit 1
179: fi
180: 
181: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
182:   echo "Warning: JAVA_HOME environment variable is not set."
183: fi
184: 
185: CLASSWORLDS_LAUNCHER=org.codehaus.plexus.classworlds.launcher.Launcher
186: 
187: # For Cygwin, switch paths to Windows format before running java
188: if $cygwin; then
189:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
190:     M2_HOME=`cygpath --path --windows "$M2_HOME"`
191:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
192:     JAVA_HOME=`cygpath --path --windows "$JAVA_HOME"`
193:   [ -n "$CLASSPATH" ] &&
194:     CLASSPATH=`cygpath --path --windows "$CLASSPATH"`
195: fi
196: 
197: # traverses directory structure from process work directory to filesystem root
198: # first directory with .mvn subdirectory is considered project base directory
199: find_maven_basedir() {
200:   local basedir=$(pwd)
201:   local wdir=$(pwd)
202:   while [ "$wdir" != '/' ] ; do
203:     if [ -d "$wdir"/.mvn ] ; then
204:       basedir=$wdir
205:       break
206:     fi
207:     wdir=$(cd "$wdir/.."; pwd)
208:   done
209:   echo "${basedir}"
210: }
211: 
212: # concatenates all lines of a file
213: concat_lines() {
214:   if [ -f "$1" ]; then
215:     echo "$(tr -s '\n' ' ' < "$1")"
216:   fi
217: }
218: 
219: export MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=${MAVEN_BASEDIR:-$(find_maven_basedir)}
220: MAVEN_OPTS="$(concat_lines "$MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR/.mvn/jvm.config") $MAVEN_OPTS"
221: 
222: # Provide a "standardized" way to retrieve the CLI args that will
223: # work with both Windows and non-Windows executions.
224: MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS="$MAVEN_CONFIG $@"
225: export MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS
226: 
227: WRAPPER_LAUNCHER=org.apache.maven.wrapper.MavenWrapperMain
228: 
229: exec "$JAVACMD" \
230:   $MAVEN_OPTS \
231:   -classpath "$MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar" \
232:   "-Dmaven.home=${M2_HOME}" "-Dmaven.multiModuleProjectDirectory=${MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR}" \
233:   ${WRAPPER_LAUNCHER} "$@"

  1: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2: @REM Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one
  3: @REM or more contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file
  4: @REM distributed with this work for additional information
  5: @REM regarding copyright ownership.  The ASF licenses this file
  6: @REM to you under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the
  7: @REM "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance
  8: @REM with the License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
  9: @REM
 10: @REM    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 11: @REM
 12: @REM Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
 13: @REM software distributed under the License is distributed on an
 14: @REM "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY
 15: @REM KIND, either express or implied.  See the License for the
 16: @REM specific language governing permissions and limitations
 17: @REM under the License.
 18: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 19: 
 20: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 21: @REM Maven2 Start Up Batch script
 22: @REM
 23: @REM Required ENV vars:
 24: @REM JAVA_HOME - location of a JDK home dir
 25: @REM
 26: @REM Optional ENV vars
 27: @REM M2_HOME - location of maven2's installed home dir
 28: @REM MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO - set to 'on' to enable the echoing of the batch commands
 29: @REM MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE - set to 'on' to wait for a key stroke before ending
 30: @REM MAVEN_OPTS - parameters passed to the Java VM when running Maven
 31: @REM     e.g. to debug Maven itself, use
 32: @REM set MAVEN_OPTS=-Xdebug -Xrunjdwp:transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=8000
 33: @REM MAVEN_SKIP_RC - flag to disable loading of mavenrc files
 34: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35: 
 36: @REM Begin all REM lines with '@' in case MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO is 'on'
 37: @echo off
 38: @REM enable echoing my setting MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO to 'on'
 39: @if "%MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO%" == "on"  echo %MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO%
 40: 
 41: @REM set %HOME% to equivalent of $HOME
 42: if "%HOME%" == "" (set "HOME=%HOMEDRIVE%%HOMEPATH%")
 43: 
 44: @REM Execute a user defined script before this one
 45: if not "%MAVEN_SKIP_RC%" == "" goto skipRcPre
 46: @REM check for pre script, once with legacy .bat ending and once with .cmd ending
 47: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.bat" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.bat"
 48: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.cmd" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.cmd"
 49: :skipRcPre
 50: 
 51: @setlocal
 52: 
 53: set ERROR_CODE=0
 54: 
 55: @REM To isolate internal variables from possible post scripts, we use another setlocal
 56: @setlocal
 57: 
 58: @REM ==== START VALIDATION ====
 59: if not "%JAVA_HOME%" == "" goto OkJHome
 60: 
 61: echo.
 62: echo Error: JAVA_HOME not found in your environment. >&2
 63: echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the >&2
 64: echo location of your Java installation. >&2
 65: echo.
 66: goto error
 67: 
 68: :OkJHome
 69: if exist "%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe" goto init
 70: 
 71: echo.
 72: echo Error: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory. >&2
 73: echo JAVA_HOME = "%JAVA_HOME%" >&2
 74: echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the >&2
 75: echo location of your Java installation. >&2
 76: echo.
 77: goto error
 78: 
 79: @REM ==== END VALIDATION ====
 80: 
 81: :init
 82: 
 83: set MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS=%*
 84: 
 85: @REM Find the project base dir, i.e. the directory that contains the folder ".mvn".
 86: @REM Fallback to current working directory if not found.
 87: 
 88: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%MAVEN_BASEDIR%
 89: IF NOT "%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%"=="" goto endDetectBaseDir
 90: 
 91: set EXEC_DIR=%CD%
 92: set WDIR=%EXEC_DIR%
 93: :findBaseDir
 94: IF EXIST "%WDIR%"\.mvn goto baseDirFound
 95: cd ..
 96: IF "%WDIR%"=="%CD%" goto baseDirNotFound
 97: set WDIR=%CD%
 98: goto findBaseDir
 99: 
100: :baseDirFound
101: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%WDIR%
102: cd "%EXEC_DIR%"
103: goto endDetectBaseDir
104: 
105: :baseDirNotFound
106: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%EXEC_DIR%
107: cd "%EXEC_DIR%"
108: 
109: :endDetectBaseDir
110: 
111: IF NOT EXIST "%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%\.mvn\jvm.config" goto endReadAdditionalConfig
112: 
113: @setlocal EnableExtensions EnableDelayedExpansion
114: for /F "usebackq delims=" %%a in ("%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%\.mvn\jvm.config") do set JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS=!JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS! %%a
115: @endlocal & set JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS=%JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS%
116: 
117: :endReadAdditionalConfig
118: 
119: SET MAVEN_JAVA_EXE="%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe"
120: 
121: set WRAPPER_JAR="".\.mvn\wrapper\maven-wrapper.jar""
122: set WRAPPER_LAUNCHER=org.apache.maven.wrapper.MavenWrapperMain
123: 
124: %MAVEN_JAVA_EXE% %JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS% %MAVEN_OPTS% %MAVEN_DEBUG_OPTS% -classpath %WRAPPER_JAR% "-Dmaven.multiModuleProjectDirectory=%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%" %WRAPPER_LAUNCHER% %MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS%
125: if ERRORLEVEL 1 goto error
126: goto end
127: 
128: :error
129: set ERROR_CODE=1
130: 
131: :end
132: @endlocal & set ERROR_CODE=%ERROR_CODE%
133: 
134: if not "%MAVEN_SKIP_RC%" == "" goto skipRcPost
135: @REM check for post script, once with legacy .bat ending and once with .cmd ending
136: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.bat" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.bat"
137: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.cmd" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.cmd"
138: :skipRcPost
139: 
140: @REM pause the script if MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE is set to 'on'
141: if "%MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE%" == "on" pause
142: 
143: if "%MAVEN_TERMINATE_CMD%" == "on" exit %ERROR_CODE%
144: 
145: exit /B %ERROR_CODE%

File: monolithic/src/main/frontend/src/app/blog-posts/blog-post-new/blog-post-new.component.ts
================
 1: import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
 2: import { Router, ActivatedRoute } from '@angular/router';
 3: import { BlogPostsService } from '../shared/blog-posts.service';
 4: import { FormGroup, Validators, FormBuilder, FormControl } from '@angular/forms';
 5: import { EventManager } from '../../shared/event-manager.service';
 6: import { BlogPostModel} from '../shared/blog-post.model';
 7: @Component({
 8:   selector: 'app-blog-post-new',
 9:   templateUrl: './blog-post-new.component.html',
10:   styleUrls: ['./blog-post-new.component.css']
11: })
12: export class BlogPostNewComponent implements OnInit {
13:    form: FormGroup;
14:    isSaving: Boolean;
15:   constructor(
16:     private blogPostsService: BlogPostsService,
17:     private route: ActivatedRoute,
18:     private router: Router,
19:     private fb: FormBuilder,
20:     private eventManager: EventManager
21:   ) {}
22:   ngOnInit() {
23:     this.form = new FormGroup({
24:     title: new FormControl(''),
25:     rawContent: new FormControl(''),
26:     publicSlug: new FormControl(''),
27:     draft: new FormControl(true),
28:     category: new FormControl(''),
29:     broadcast: new FormControl(true),
30:     publishAt: new FormControl('')
31:   });
32:   }
33:   onSubmit({ value, valid }: { value: BlogPostModel, valid: boolean }) {
34:       let ngbDate = this.form.controls['publishAt'].value;
35:       value.publishAt = new Date(ngbDate.year, ngbDate.month - 1, ngbDate.day);
36:       this.blogPostsService.addBlogPost(value).subscribe(response => this.onSaveSuccess(response), () => this.onSaveError());
37:     }
38:     private onSaveSuccess(result) {
39:         this.eventManager.broadcast({ name: 'blogPostListModification', content: 'OK' });
40:         this.isSaving = false;
41:     }
42:     private onSaveError() {
43:         this.isSaving = false;
44:     }
45: }

 1: import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';
 2: import { BlogPostsService } from '../shared/blog-posts.service';
 3: import { BlogPostModel } from '../shared/blog-post.model';
 4: import { Router, ActivatedRoute, Params } from '@angular/router';
 5: import 'rxjs/add/operator/switchMap';
 6: import 'rxjs/add/operator/filter';
 7: @Component({
 8:   selector: 'app-blog-post',
 9:   templateUrl: './blog-post.component.html',
10:   styleUrls: ['./blog-post.component.css']
11: })
12: export class BlogPostComponent implements OnInit {
13:   blogPost: BlogPostModel;
14:   errorMessage: string;
15:   navigated = false;
16:   constructor(
17:     private blogPostsService: BlogPostsService,
18:     private route: ActivatedRoute,
19:     private router: Router
20:   ) {  }
21:   ngOnInit() {
22:     this.route.params.forEach((params: Params) => {
23:       if (params['id'] !== undefined) {
24:         let id = params['id'];
25:         this.navigated = true;
26:         this.getBlogPost(id);
27:       } else {
28:         this.navigated = false;
29:         this.blogPost = new BlogPostModel();
30:       }
31:      });
32:     }
33:   private getBlogPost(id: string): void {
34:     this.blogPostsService.getBlogPost(id).subscribe(
35:                                       blogPost => this.blogPost = blogPost,
36:                                       error =>  this.errorMessage = <any>error);
37:   }
38: }

 9: export class BlogPostsService {

14:     let body = res.json();
15:     return body._embedded.blogposts || { };
16:   }
17:   private extractSingleData(res: Response) {
18:     let body = res.json();
19:     return body || { };
20:   }

26:   }

File: monolithic/src/main/frontend/src/app/shared/alert/alert.service.ts
================
  1: import { Injectable, Sanitizer, SecurityContext } from '@angular/core';
  2: @Injectable()
  3: export class AlertService {
  4:     private alertId: number;
  5:     private alerts: any[];
  6:     private timeout: number;
  7:     constructor(private sanitizer: Sanitizer, private toast: boolean) {
  8:         this.alertId = 0;
  9:         this.alerts = [];
 10:         this.timeout = 5000;
 11:     }
 12:     clear() {
 13:         this.alerts = [];
 14:     }
 15:     get(): any {
 16:         return this.alerts;
 17:     }
 18:     success(msg, params, position): any {
 19:         return this.addAlert({
 20:             type: 'success',
 21:             msg: msg,
 22:             params: params,
 23:             timeout: this.timeout,
 24:             toast: this.toast,
 25:             position: position
 26:         }, []);
 27:     }
 28:     error(msg, params, position): any {
 29:         return this.addAlert({
 30:             type: 'danger',
 31:             msg: msg,
 32:             params: params,
 33:             timeout: this.timeout,
 34:             toast: this.toast,
 35:             position: position
 36:         }, []);
 37:     }
 38:     warning(msg, params, position): any {
 39:         return this.addAlert({
 40:             type: 'warning',
 41:             msg: msg,
 42:             params: params,
 43:             timeout: this.timeout,
 44:             toast: this.toast,
 45:             position: position
 46:         }, []);
 47:     }
 48:     info(msg, params, position): any {
 49:         return this.addAlert({
 50:             type: 'info',
 51:             msg: msg,
 52:             params: params,
 53:             timeout: this.timeout,
 54:             toast: this.toast,
 55:             position: position
 56:         }, []);
 57:     }
 58:     factory(alertOptions): any {
 59:         let alert = {
 60:             type: alertOptions.type,
 61:             msg: this.sanitizer.sanitize(SecurityContext.HTML, alertOptions.msg),
 62:             id: alertOptions.alertId,
 63:             timeout: alertOptions.timeout,
 64:             toast: alertOptions.toast,
 65:             position: alertOptions.position ? alertOptions.position : 'top right',
 66:             scoped: alertOptions.scoped,
 67:             close: function (alerts) {
 68:                 return this.closeAlert(this.id, alerts);
 69:             }
 70:         };
 71:         if (!alert.scoped) {
 72:             this.alerts.push(alert);
 73:         }
 74:         return alert;
 75:     }
 76:     addAlert(alertOptions, extAlerts): any {
 77:         alertOptions.alertId = this.alertId++;
 78:         if (alertOptions.msg !== undefined) {
 79:         }
 80:         let alert = this.factory(alertOptions);
 81:         if (alertOptions.timeout && alertOptions.timeout > 0) {
 82:             setTimeout(() => {
 83:                 this.closeAlert(alertOptions.alertId, extAlerts);
 84:             }, alertOptions.timeout);
 85:         }
 86:         return alert;
 87:     }
 88:     closeAlert(id, extAlerts): any {
 89:         let thisAlerts = extAlerts ? extAlerts : this.alerts;
 90:         return this.closeAlertByIndex(thisAlerts.map(function (e) {
 91:             return e.id;
 92:         }).indexOf(id), thisAlerts);
 93:     }
 94:     closeAlertByIndex(index, thisAlerts): any {
 95:         return thisAlerts.splice(index, 1);
 96:     }
 97:     isToast(): boolean {
 98:         return this.toast;
 99:     }
100: }

File: monolithic/src/main/frontend/src/app/shared/event-manager.service.ts
================
 1: import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
 2: import { Observable, Observer, Subscription} from 'rxjs/Rx';
 3: @Injectable()
 4: export class EventManager {
 5:     observable: Observable<any>;
 6:     observer: Observer<any>;
 7:     constructor() {
 8:         this.observable = Observable.create((observer: Observer<any>) => {
 9:             this.observer = observer;
10:         }).share();
11:     }
12:     broadcast(event) {
13:         this.observer.next(event);
14:     }
15:     subscribe(eventName, callback) {
16:         let subscriber: Subscription = this.observable.filter((event) => {
17:             return event.name === eventName;
18:         }).subscribe(callback);
19:         return subscriber;
20:     }
21:     destroy(subscriber: Subscription) {
22:         subscriber.unsubscribe();
23:     }
24: }

 1: import { HttpInterceptable } from './http.interceptable';
 2: import { RequestOptionsArgs, Response } from '@angular/http';
 3: import { Observable } from 'rxjs/Observable';
 4: import { EventManager } from '../../shared/event-manager.service';
 5: export class ErrorHandlerInterceptor extends HttpInterceptable {
 6:     constructor(private eventManager: EventManager) {
 7:         super();
 8:     }
 9:     requestIntercept(options?: RequestOptionsArgs): RequestOptionsArgs {
10:         return options;
11:     }
12:     responseIntercept(observable: Observable<Response>): Observable<Response> {
13:         return <Observable<Response>> observable.catch(error => {
14:             if (!(error.status === 401)) {
15:                 console.error('HTTP Error broadcasted:');
16:                 console.error(error);
17:                 this.eventManager.broadcast( {name: 'microcompanyuiApp.httpError', content: error});
18:             }
19:             return Observable.throw(error);
20:         });
21:     }
22: }

File: monolithic/src/main/frontend/src/app/shared/interceptor/http.interceptable.ts
================
 1: import { Observable } from 'rxjs/Observable';
 2: import { Response, RequestOptionsArgs } from '@angular/http';
 3: export abstract class HttpInterceptable {
 4:     private _successor: HttpInterceptable = null;
 5:     set successor(successor: HttpInterceptable) {
 6:         this._successor = successor;
 7:     }
 8:     processRequestInterception(options?: RequestOptionsArgs): RequestOptionsArgs {
 9:         return (!this._successor) ? this.requestIntercept(options) :
10:             this._successor.processRequestInterception(this.requestIntercept(options));
11:     }
12:     processResponseInterception(response: Observable<Response>): Observable<Response> {
13:         return (!this._successor) ? this.responseIntercept(response) :
14:             this._successor.processResponseInterception(this.responseIntercept(response));
15:     }
16:     abstract requestIntercept(options?: RequestOptionsArgs): RequestOptionsArgs;
17:     abstract responseIntercept(observable: Observable<Response>): Observable<Response>;
18: }

================
File: monolithic/src/main/frontend/src/app/shared/interceptor/http.interceptor.ts
================
 1: import { HttpInterceptable } from './http.interceptable';
 2: import { Injectable } from '@angular/core';
 3: import { Http, ConnectionBackend, RequestOptions, RequestOptionsArgs, Request, Response, Headers } from '@angular/http';
 4: import { Observable } from 'rxjs/Observable';
 5: @Injectable()
 6: export class HttpInterceptor extends Http {
 7:     private firstInterceptor: HttpInterceptable;
 8:     constructor(
 9:         backend: ConnectionBackend,
10:         defaultOptions: RequestOptions,
11:         interceptors: HttpInterceptable[]
12:     ) {
13:         super(backend, defaultOptions);
14:         if (interceptors.length > 0) {
15:             interceptors.reduce((chain, current) => {
16:                 chain.successor = current;
17:                 return current;
18:             });
19:             this.firstInterceptor = interceptors[0];
20:         }
21:     }
22:     request(url: string | Request, options?: RequestOptionsArgs): Observable<Response> {
23:         return this.intercept(super.request(url, this.getRequestOptionArgs(options)));
24:     }
25:     get(url: string, options?: RequestOptionsArgs): Observable<Response> {
26:         return super.get(url, this.getRequestOptionArgs(options));
27:     }
28:     post(url: string, body: string, options?: RequestOptionsArgs): Observable<Response> {
29:         return super.post(url, body, this.getRequestOptionArgs(options));
30:     }
31:     put(url: string, body: string, options?: RequestOptionsArgs): Observable<Response> {
32:         return super.put(url, body, this.getRequestOptionArgs(options));
33:     }
34:     delete(url: string, options?: RequestOptionsArgs): Observable<Response> {
35:         return super.delete(url, this.getRequestOptionArgs(options));
36:     }
37:     getRequestOptionArgs(options?: RequestOptionsArgs): RequestOptionsArgs {
38:         if (options == null) {
39:             options = new RequestOptions();
40:         }
41:         if (options.headers == null) {
42:             options.headers = new Headers();
43:         }
44:         return !this.firstInterceptor ? options : this.firstInterceptor.processRequestInterception(options);
45:     }
46:     intercept(observable: Observable<Response>): Observable<Response> {
47:         return !this.firstInterceptor ? observable : this.firstInterceptor.processResponseInterception(observable);
48:     }
49: }

 9656: /**
 9657:  * A regular expression for breaking a URI into its component parts.
 9658:  *
 9659:  * {@link http://www.gbiv.com/protocols/uri/rfc/rfc3986.html#RFC2234} says
 9660:  * As the "first-match-wins" algorithm is identical to the "greedy"
 9661:  * disambiguation method used by POSIX regular expressions, it is natural and
 9662:  * commonplace to use a regular expression for parsing the potential five
 9663:  * components of a URI reference.
 9664:  *
 9665:  * The following line is the regular expression for breaking-down a
 9666:  * well-formed URI reference into its components.
 9667:  *
 9668:  * <pre>
 9669:  * ^(([^:/?#]+):)?(//([^/?#]*))?([^?#]*)(\?([^#]*))?(#(.*))?
 9670:  *  12            3  4          5       6  7        8 9
 9671:  * </pre>
 9672:  *
 9673:  * The numbers in the second line above are only to assist readability; they
 9674:  * indicate the reference points for each subexpression (i.e., each paired
 9675:  * parenthesis). We refer to the value matched for subexpression <n> as $<n>.
 9676:  * For example, matching the above expression to
 9677:  * <pre>
 9678:  *     http://www.ics.uci.edu/pub/ietf/uri/#Related
 9679:  * </pre>
 9680:  * results in the following subexpression matches:
 9681:  * <pre>
 9682:  *    $1 = http:
 9683:  *    $2 = http
 9684:  *    $3 = //www.ics.uci.edu
 9685:  *    $4 = www.ics.uci.edu
 9686:  *    $5 = /pub/ietf/uri/
 9687:  *    $6 = <undefined>
 9688:  *    $7 = <undefined>
 9689:  *    $8 = #Related
 9690:  *    $9 = Related
 9691:  * </pre>
 9692:  * where <undefined> indicates that the component is not present, as is the
 9693:  * case for the query component in the above example. Therefore, we can
 9694:  * determine the value of the five components as
 9695:  * <pre>
 9696:  *    scheme    = $2
 9697:  *    authority = $4
 9698:  *    path      = $5
 9699:  *    query     = $7
 9700:  *    fragment  = $9
 9701:  * </pre>
 9702:  *
 9703:  * The regular expression has been modified slightly to expose the
 9704:  * userInfo, domain, and port separately from the authority.
 9705:  * The modified version yields
 9706:  * <pre>
 9707:  *    $1 = http              scheme
 9708:  *    $2 = <undefined>       userInfo -\
 9709:  *    $3 = www.ics.uci.edu   domain     | authority
 9710:  *    $4 = <undefined>       port     -/
 9711:  *    $5 = /pub/ietf/uri/    path
 9712:  *    $6 = <undefined>       query without ?
 9713:  *    $7 = Related           fragment without #
 9714:  * </pre>
 9715:  * @type {!RegExp}
 9716:  * @internal
 9717:  */

19891: /**

19931: function utf8Encode(str) {
19932:     var encoded = '';
19933:     for (var index = 0; index < str.length; index++) {
19934:         var codePoint = decodeSurrogatePairs(str, index);
19935:         if (codePoint <= 0x7f) {
19936:             encoded += String.fromCharCode(codePoint);
19937:         }
19938:         else if (codePoint <= 0x7ff) {
19939:             encoded += String.fromCharCode(0xc0 | codePoint >>> 6, 0x80 | codePoint & 0x3f);
19940:         }
19941:         else if (codePoint <= 0xffff) {
19942:             encoded += String.fromCharCode(0xe0 | codePoint >>> 12, 0x80 | codePoint >>> 6 & 0x3f, 0x80 | codePoint & 0x3f);
19943:         }
19944:         else if (codePoint <= 0x1fffff) {
19945:             encoded += String.fromCharCode(0xf0 | codePoint >>> 18, 0x80 | codePoint >>> 12 & 0x3f, 0x80 | codePoint >>> 6 & 0x3f, 0x80 | codePoint & 0x3f);
19946:         }
19947:     }
19948:     return encoded;
19949: }
19950: // see https://mathiasbynens.be/notes/javascript-encoding#surrogate-formulae
19951: function decodeSurrogatePairs(str, index) {
19952:     if (index < 0 || index >= str.length) {
19953:         throw new Error("index=" + index + " is out of range in \"" + str + "\"");
19954:     }
19955:     var high = str.charCodeAt(index);
19956:     var low;
19957:     if (high >= 0xd800 && high <= 0xdfff && str.length > index + 1) {
19958:         low = str.charCodeAt(index + 1);
19959:         if (low >= 0xdc00 && low <= 0xdfff) {
19960:             return (high - 0xd800) * 0x400 + low - 0xdc00 + 0x10000;
19961:         }
19962:     }
19963:     return high;
19964: }
19965: function stringToWords32(str) {
19966:     var words32 = Array(str.length >>> 2);
19967:     for (var i = 0; i < words32.length; i++) {
19968:         words32[i] = 0;
19969:     }
19970:     for (var i = 0; i < str.length; i++) {
19971:         words32[i >>> 2] |= (str.charCodeAt(i) & 0xff) << 8 * (3 - i & 0x3);
19972:     }
19973:     return words32;
19974: }
19975: function words32ToString(words32) {
19976:     var str = '';
19977:     for (var i = 0; i < words32.length * 4; i++) {
19978:         str += String.fromCharCode((words32[i >>> 2] >>> 8 * (3 - i & 0x3)) & 0xff);
19979:     }
19980:     return str;
19981: }
19982: function fk(index, b, c, d) {
19983:     if (index < 20) {
19984:         return [(b & c) | (~b & d), 0x5a827999];
19985:     }
19986:     if (index < 40) {
19987:         return [b ^ c ^ d, 0x6ed9eba1];
19988:     }
19989:     if (index < 60) {
19990:         return [(b & c) | (b & d) | (c & d), 0x8f1bbcdc];
19991:     }
19992:     return [b ^ c ^ d, 0xca62c1d6];
19993: }
19994: function add32(a, b) {
19995:     var low = (a & 0xffff) + (b & 0xffff);
19996:     var high = (a >> 16) + (b >> 16) + (low >> 16);
19997:     return (high << 16) | (low & 0xffff);
19998: }
19999: function rol32(a, count) {
20000:     return (a << count) | (a >>> (32 - count));
20001: }

43622: var Trigger = (function () {
43623:     function Trigger(open, close) {
43624:         this.open = open;
43625:         this.close = close;
43626:         if (!close) {
43627:             this.close = open;
43628:         }
43629:     }
43630:     Trigger.prototype.isManual = function () { return this.open === 'manual' || this.close === 'manual'; };
43631:     return Trigger;
43632: }());
43633: var DEFAULT_ALIASES = {
43634:     hover: ['mouseenter', 'mouseleave']
43635: };
43636: function parseTriggers(triggers, aliases) {
43637:     if (aliases === void 0) { aliases = DEFAULT_ALIASES; }
43638:     var trimmedTriggers = (triggers || '').trim();
43639:     if (trimmedTriggers.length === 0) {
43640:         return [];
43641:     }
43642:     var parsedTriggers = trimmedTriggers.split(/\s+/).map(function (trigger) { return trigger.split(':'); }).map(function (triggerPair) {
43643:         var alias = aliases[triggerPair[0]] || triggerPair;
43644:         return new Trigger(alias[0], alias[1]);
43645:     });
43646:     var manualTriggers = parsedTriggers.filter(function (triggerPair) { return triggerPair.isManual(); });
43647:     if (manualTriggers.length > 1) {
43648:         throw 'Triggers parse error: only one manual trigger is allowed';
43649:     }
43650:     if (manualTriggers.length === 1 && parsedTriggers.length > 1) {
43651:         throw 'Triggers parse error: manual trigger can\'t be mixed with other triggers';
43652:     }
43653:     return parsedTriggers;
43654: }
43655: var noopFn = function () { };
43656: function listenToTriggers(renderer, nativeElement, triggers, openFn, closeFn, toggleFn) {
43657:     var parsedTriggers = parseTriggers(triggers);
43658:     var listeners = [];
43659:     if (parsedTriggers.length === 1 && parsedTriggers[0].isManual()) {
43660:         return noopFn;
43661:     }
43662:     parsedTriggers.forEach(function (trigger) {
43663:         if (trigger.open === trigger.close) {
43664:             listeners.push(renderer.listen(nativeElement, trigger.open, toggleFn));
43665:         }
43666:         else {
43667:             listeners.push(renderer.listen(nativeElement, trigger.open, openFn), renderer.listen(nativeElement, trigger.close, closeFn));
43668:         }
43669:     });
43670:     return function () { listeners.forEach(function (unsubscribeFn) { return unsubscribeFn(); }); };

66525: function chooseLocale(names) {
66526:     var i = 0, j, next, locale, split;
66527:     while (i < names.length) {
66528:         split = normalizeLocale(names[i]).split('-');
66529:         j = split.length;
66530:         next = normalizeLocale(names[i + 1]);
66531:         next = next ? next.split('-') : null;
66532:         while (j > 0) {
66533:             locale = loadLocale(split.slice(0, j).join('-'));
66534:             if (locale) {
66535:                 return locale;
66536:             }
66537:             if (next && next.length >= j && compareArrays(split, next, true) >= j - 1) {
66538:                 break;
66539:             }
66540:             j--;
66541:         }
66542:         i++;
66543:     }
66544:     return null;
66545: }

66653: function checkOverflow (m) {
66654:     var overflow;
66655:     var a = m._a;
66656:     if (a && getParsingFlags(m).overflow === -2) {
66657:         overflow =
66658:             a[MONTH]       < 0 || a[MONTH]       > 11  ? MONTH :
66659:             a[DATE]        < 1 || a[DATE]        > daysInMonth(a[YEAR], a[MONTH]) ? DATE :
66660:             a[HOUR]        < 0 || a[HOUR]        > 24 || (a[HOUR] === 24 && (a[MINUTE] !== 0 || a[SECOND] !== 0 || a[MILLISECOND] !== 0)) ? HOUR :
66661:             a[MINUTE]      < 0 || a[MINUTE]      > 59  ? MINUTE :
66662:             a[SECOND]      < 0 || a[SECOND]      > 59  ? SECOND :
66663:             a[MILLISECOND] < 0 || a[MILLISECOND] > 999 ? MILLISECOND :
66664:             -1;
66665:         if (getParsingFlags(m)._overflowDayOfYear && (overflow < YEAR || overflow > DATE)) {
66666:             overflow = DATE;
66667:         }
66668:         if (getParsingFlags(m)._overflowWeeks && overflow === -1) {
66669:             overflow = WEEK;
66670:         }
66671:         if (getParsingFlags(m)._overflowWeekday && overflow === -1) {
66672:             overflow = WEEKDAY;
66673:         }
66674:         getParsingFlags(m).overflow = overflow;
66675:     }
66676:     return m;

66794: // convert an array to a date.
66795: // the array should mirror the parameters below
66796: // note: all values past the year are optional and will default to the lowest possible value.
66797: // [year, month, day , hour, minute, second, millisecond]
66798: function configFromArray (config) {
66799:     var i, date, input = [], currentDate, yearToUse;
66800:     if (config._d) {
66801:         return;
66802:     }
66803:     currentDate = currentDateArray(config);
66804:     //compute day of the year from weeks and weekdays
66805:     if (config._w && config._a[DATE] == null && config._a[MONTH] == null) {
66806:         dayOfYearFromWeekInfo(config);
66807:     }
66808:     //if the day of the year is set, figure out what it is
66809:     if (config._dayOfYear) {
66810:         yearToUse = defaults(config._a[YEAR], currentDate[YEAR]);
66811:         if (config._dayOfYear > daysInYear(yearToUse)) {
66812:             getParsingFlags(config)._overflowDayOfYear = true;
66813:         }
66814:         date = createUTCDate(yearToUse, 0, config._dayOfYear);
66815:         config._a[MONTH] = date.getUTCMonth();
66816:         config._a[DATE] = date.getUTCDate();
66817:     }
66818:     // Default to current date.
66819:     // * if no year, month, day of month are given, default to today
66820:     // * if day of month is given, default month and year
66821:     // * if month is given, default only year
66822:     // * if year is given, don't default anything
66823:     for (i = 0; i < 3 && config._a[i] == null; ++i) {
66824:         config._a[i] = input[i] = currentDate[i];
66825:     }
66826:     for (; i < 7; i++) {
66827:         config._a[i] = input[i] = (config._a[i] == null) ? (i === 2 ? 1 : 0) : config._a[i];
66828:     }
66829:     if (config._a[HOUR] === 24 &&
66830:             config._a[MINUTE] === 0 &&
66831:             config._a[SECOND] === 0 &&
66832:             config._a[MILLISECOND] === 0) {
66833:         config._nextDay = true;
66834:         config._a[HOUR] = 0;
66835:     }
66836:     config._d = (config._useUTC ? createUTCDate : createDate).apply(null, input);
66837:     if (config._tzm != null) {
66838:         config._d.setUTCMinutes(config._d.getUTCMinutes() - config._tzm);
66839:     }
66840:     if (config._nextDay) {
66841:         config._a[HOUR] = 24;
66842:     }
66843: }
66844: function dayOfYearFromWeekInfo(config) {
66845:     var w, weekYear, week, weekday, dow, doy, temp, weekdayOverflow;
66846:     w = config._w;
66847:     if (w.GG != null || w.W != null || w.E != null) {
66848:         dow = 1;
66849:         doy = 4;
66850:         weekYear = defaults(w.GG, config._a[YEAR], weekOfYear(createLocal(), 1, 4).year);
66851:         week = defaults(w.W, 1);
66852:         weekday = defaults(w.E, 1);
66853:         if (weekday < 1 || weekday > 7) {
66854:             weekdayOverflow = true;
66855:         }
66856:     } else {
66857:         dow = config._locale._week.dow;
66858:         doy = config._locale._week.doy;
66859:         var curWeek = weekOfYear(createLocal(), dow, doy);
66860:         weekYear = defaults(w.gg, config._a[YEAR], curWeek.year);
66861:         week = defaults(w.w, curWeek.week);
66862:         if (w.d != null) {
66863:             weekday = w.d;
66864:             if (weekday < 0 || weekday > 6) {
66865:                 weekdayOverflow = true;
66866:             }
66867:         } else if (w.e != null) {
66868:             weekday = w.e + dow;
66869:             if (w.e < 0 || w.e > 6) {
66870:                 weekdayOverflow = true;
66871:             }
66872:         } else {
66873:             weekday = dow;
66874:         }
66875:     }
66876:     if (week < 1 || week > weeksInYear(weekYear, dow, doy)) {
66877:         getParsingFlags(config)._overflowWeeks = true;
66878:     } else if (weekdayOverflow != null) {
66879:         getParsingFlags(config)._overflowWeekday = true;
66880:     } else {
66881:         temp = dayOfYearFromWeeks(weekYear, week, weekday, dow, doy);
66882:         config._a[YEAR] = temp.year;
66883:         config._dayOfYear = temp.dayOfYear;
66884:     }

66939: function meridiemFixWrap (locale, hour, meridiem) {

67009: function prepareConfig (config) {
67010:     var input = config._i,
67011:         format = config._f;
67012:     config._locale = config._locale || getLocale(config._l);
67013:     if (input === null || (format === undefined && input === '')) {
67014:         return createInvalid({nullInput: true});
67015:     }
67016:     if (typeof input === 'string') {
67017:         config._i = input = config._locale.preparse(input);
67018:     }
67019:     if (isMoment(input)) {
67020:         return new Moment(checkOverflow(input));
67021:     } else if (isDate(input)) {
67022:         config._d = input;
67023:     } else if (isArray(format)) {
67024:         configFromStringAndArray(config);
67025:     } else if (format) {
67026:         configFromStringAndFormat(config);
67027:     }  else {
67028:         configFromInput(config);
67029:     }
67030:     if (!isValid(config)) {
67031:         config._d = null;

67033:     return config;

67035: function configFromInput(config) {
67036:     var input = config._i;
67037:     if (input === undefined) {
67038:         config._d = new Date(hooks.now());
67039:     } else if (isDate(input)) {
67040:         config._d = new Date(input.valueOf());
67041:     } else if (typeof input === 'string') {
67042:         configFromString(config);
67043:     } else if (isArray(input)) {
67044:         config._a = map(input.slice(0), function (obj) {
67045:             return parseInt(obj, 10);
67046:         });
67047:         configFromArray(config);
67048:     } else if (typeof(input) === 'object') {
67049:         configFromObject(config);
67050:     } else if (isNumber(input)) {
67051:         config._d = new Date(input);
67052:     } else {
67053:         hooks.createFromInputFallback(config);
67054:     }

67180: var chunkOffset = /([\+\-]|\d\d)/gi;
67181: function offsetFromString(matcher, string) {
67182:     var matches = (string || '').match(matcher);
67183:     if (matches === null) {
67184:         return null;
67185:     }
67186:     var chunk   = matches[matches.length - 1] || [];
67187:     var parts   = (chunk + '').match(chunkOffset) || ['-', 0, 0];
67188:     var minutes = +(parts[1] * 60) + toInt(parts[2]);
67189:     return minutes === 0 ?
67190:       0 :
67191:       parts[0] === '+' ? minutes : -minutes;

67335: function createDuration (input, key) {
67336:     var duration = input,
67337:         match = null,
67338:         sign,
67339:         ret,
67340:         diffRes;
67341:     if (isDuration(input)) {
67342:         duration = {
67343:             ms : input._milliseconds,
67344:             d  : input._days,
67345:             M  : input._months
67346:         };
67347:     } else if (isNumber(input)) {
67348:         duration = {};
67349:         if (key) {
67350:             duration[key] = input;
67351:         } else {
67352:             duration.milliseconds = input;
67353:         }
67354:     } else if (!!(match = aspNetRegex.exec(input))) {
67355:         sign = (match[1] === '-') ? -1 : 1;
67356:         duration = {
67357:             y  : 0,
67358:             d  : toInt(match[DATE])                         * sign,
67359:             h  : toInt(match[HOUR])                         * sign,
67360:             m  : toInt(match[MINUTE])                       * sign,
67361:             s  : toInt(match[SECOND])                       * sign,
67362:             ms : toInt(absRound(match[MILLISECOND] * 1000)) * sign
67363:         };
67364:     } else if (!!(match = isoRegex.exec(input))) {
67365:         sign = (match[1] === '-') ? -1 : 1;
67366:         duration = {
67367:             y : parseIso(match[2], sign),
67368:             M : parseIso(match[3], sign),
67369:             w : parseIso(match[4], sign),
67370:             d : parseIso(match[5], sign),
67371:             h : parseIso(match[6], sign),
67372:             m : parseIso(match[7], sign),
67373:             s : parseIso(match[8], sign)
67374:         };
67375:     } else if (duration == null) {
67376:         duration = {};
67377:     } else if (typeof duration === 'object' && ('from' in duration || 'to' in duration)) {
67378:         diffRes = momentsDifference(createLocal(duration.from), createLocal(duration.to));
67379:         duration = {};
67380:         duration.ms = diffRes.milliseconds;
67381:         duration.M = diffRes.months;
67382:     }
67383:     ret = new Duration(duration);
67384:     if (isDuration(input) && hasOwnProp(input, '_locale')) {
67385:         ret._locale = input._locale;
67386:     }
67387:     return ret;
67388: }

67390: function parseIso (inp, sign) {
67391:     var res = inp && parseFloat(inp.replace(',', '.'));
67392:     return (isNaN(res) ? 0 : res) * sign;
67393: }
67394: function positiveMomentsDifference(base, other) {
67395:     var res = {milliseconds: 0, months: 0};
67396:     res.months = other.month() - base.month() +
67397:         (other.year() - base.year()) * 12;
67398:     if (base.clone().add(res.months, 'M').isAfter(other)) {
67399:         --res.months;
67400:     }
67401:     res.milliseconds = +other - +(base.clone().add(res.months, 'M'));
67402:     return res;

67404: function momentsDifference(base, other) {
67405:     var res;
67406:     if (!(base.isValid() && other.isValid())) {
67407:         return {milliseconds: 0, months: 0};
67408:     }
67409:     other = cloneWithOffset(other, base);
67410:     if (base.isBefore(other)) {
67411:         res = positiveMomentsDifference(base, other);
67412:     } else {

67414:         res.milliseconds = -res.milliseconds;
67415:         res.months = -res.months;
67416:     }
67417:     return res;

67419: function createAdder(direction, name) {

67421:         var dur, tmp;

67423:             deprecateSimple(name, 'moment().' + name  + '(period, number) is deprecated. Please use moment().' + name + '(number, period). ' +

67524: function diff (input, units, asFloat) {
67525:     var that,
67526:         zoneDelta,
67527:         delta, output;
67528:     if (!this.isValid()) {
67529:         return NaN;
67530:     }
67531:     that = cloneWithOffset(input, this);
67532:     if (!that.isValid()) {
67533:         return NaN;
67534:     }
67535:     zoneDelta = (that.utcOffset() - this.utcOffset()) * 6e4;
67536:     units = normalizeUnits(units);
67537:     if (units === 'year' || units === 'month' || units === 'quarter') {
67538:         output = monthDiff(this, that);
67539:         if (units === 'quarter') {
67540:             output = output / 3;
67541:         } else if (units === 'year') {
67542:             output = output / 12;
67543:         }
67544:     } else {
67545:         delta = this - that;
67546:         output = units === 'second' ? delta / 1e3 :
67547:             units === 'minute' ? delta / 6e4 :
67548:             units === 'hour' ? delta / 36e5 :
67549:             units === 'day' ? (delta - zoneDelta) / 864e5 :
67550:             units === 'week' ? (delta - zoneDelta) / 6048e5 :
67551:             delta;
67552:     }
67553:     return asFloat ? output : absFloor(output);
67554: }
67555: function monthDiff (a, b) {
67556:     var wholeMonthDiff = ((b.year() - a.year()) * 12) + (b.month() - a.month()),
67557:         anchor = a.clone().add(wholeMonthDiff, 'months'),
67558:         anchor2, adjust;
67559:     if (b - anchor < 0) {
67560:         anchor2 = a.clone().add(wholeMonthDiff - 1, 'months');
67561:         adjust = (b - anchor) / (anchor - anchor2);
67562:     } else {
67563:         anchor2 = a.clone().add(wholeMonthDiff + 1, 'months');
67564:         adjust = (b - anchor) / (anchor2 - anchor);
67565:     }
67566:     return -(wholeMonthDiff + adjust) || 0;
67567: }

68144:         return Math.floor(number);

68149: function bubble () {
68150:     var milliseconds = this._milliseconds;
68151:     var days         = this._days;
68152:     var months       = this._months;
68153:     var data         = this._data;
68154:     var seconds, minutes, hours, years, monthsFromDays;
68155:     if (!((milliseconds >= 0 && days >= 0 && months >= 0) ||
68156:             (milliseconds <= 0 && days <= 0 && months <= 0))) {
68157:         milliseconds += absCeil(monthsToDays(months) + days) * 864e5;
68158:         days = 0;
68159:         months = 0;
68160:     }
68161:     data.milliseconds = milliseconds % 1000;
68162:     seconds           = absFloor(milliseconds / 1000);
68163:     data.seconds      = seconds % 60;
68164:     minutes           = absFloor(seconds / 60);
68165:     data.minutes      = minutes % 60;
68166:     hours             = absFloor(minutes / 60);
68167:     data.hours        = hours % 24;
68168:     days += absFloor(hours / 24);
68169:     monthsFromDays = absFloor(daysToMonths(days));
68170:     months += monthsFromDays;
68171:     days -= absCeil(monthsToDays(monthsFromDays));
68172:     years = absFloor(months / 12);
68173:     months %= 12;
68174:     data.days   = days;
68175:     data.months = months;
68176:     data.years  = years;
68177:     return this;
68178: }
68179: function daysToMonths (days) {
68180:     return days * 4800 / 146097;
68181: }
68182: function monthsToDays (months) {
68183:     return months * 146097 / 4800;

68185: function as (units) {
68186:     var days;
68187:     var months;
68188:     var milliseconds = this._milliseconds;
68189:     units = normalizeUnits(units);
68190:     if (units === 'month' || units === 'year') {
68191:         days   = this._days   + milliseconds / 864e5;
68192:         months = this._months + daysToMonths(days);
68193:         return units === 'month' ? months : months / 12;
68194:     } else {
68195:         days = this._days + Math.round(monthsToDays(this._months));
68196:         switch (units) {
68197:             case 'week'   : return days / 7     + milliseconds / 6048e5;
68198:             case 'day'    : return days         + milliseconds / 864e5;
68199:             case 'hour'   : return days * 24    + milliseconds / 36e5;
68200:             case 'minute' : return days * 1440  + milliseconds / 6e4;
68201:             case 'second' : return days * 86400 + milliseconds / 1000;
68202:             case 'millisecond': return Math.floor(days * 864e5) + milliseconds;
68203:             default: throw new Error('Unknown unit ' + units);
68204:         }
68205:     }
68206: }

 62: 				domStyle.parts.push(addStyle(item.parts[j], options));
 63: 			}
 64: 		} else {
 65: 			var parts = [];
 66: 			for(var j = 0; j < item.parts.length; j++) {
 67: 				parts.push(addStyle(item.parts[j], options));
 68: 			}
 69: 			stylesInDom[item.id] = {id: item.id, refs: 1, parts: parts};
 70: 		}
 71: 	}
 72: }
 73: function listToStyles(list) {
 74: 	var styles = [];
 75: 	var newStyles = {};
 76: 	for(var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
 77: 		var item = list[i];
 78: 		var id = item[0];
 79: 		var css = item[1];
 80: 		var media = item[2];
 81: 		var sourceMap = item[3];
 82: 		var part = {css: css, media: media, sourceMap: sourceMap};
 83: 		if(!newStyles[id])
 84: 			styles.push(newStyles[id] = {id: id, parts: [part]});
 85: 		else
 86: 			newStyles[id].parts.push(part);
 87: 	}
 88: 	return styles;
 89: }
 90: function insertStyleElement(options, styleElement) {
 91: 	var head = getHeadElement();
 92: 	var lastStyleElementInsertedAtTop = styleElementsInsertedAtTop[styleElementsInsertedAtTop.length - 1];
 93: 	if (options.insertAt === "top") {
 94: 		if(!lastStyleElementInsertedAtTop) {
 95: 			head.insertBefore(styleElement, head.firstChild);
 96: 		} else if(lastStyleElementInsertedAtTop.nextSibling) {
 97: 			head.insertBefore(styleElement, lastStyleElementInsertedAtTop.nextSibling);
 98: 		} else {
 99: 			head.appendChild(styleElement);
100: 		}
101: 		styleElementsInsertedAtTop.push(styleElement);
102: 	} else if (options.insertAt === "bottom") {
103: 		head.appendChild(styleElement);
104: 	} else {
105: 		throw new Error("Invalid value for parameter 'insertAt'. Must be 'top' or 'bottom'.");
106: 	}
107: }
108: function removeStyleElement(styleElement) {
109: 	styleElement.parentNode.removeChild(styleElement);
110: 	var idx = styleElementsInsertedAtTop.indexOf(styleElement);
111: 	if(idx >= 0) {
112: 		styleElementsInsertedAtTop.splice(idx, 1);
113: 	}
114: }
115: function createStyleElement(options) {
116: 	var styleElement = document.createElement("style");
117: 	styleElement.type = "text/css";
118: 	insertStyleElement(options, styleElement);
119: 	return styleElement;
120: }
121: function createLinkElement(options) {
122: 	var linkElement = document.createElement("link");
123: 	linkElement.rel = "stylesheet";
124: 	insertStyleElement(options, linkElement);
125: 	return linkElement;
126: }
127: function addStyle(obj, options) {
128: 	var styleElement, update, remove;
129: 	if (options.singleton) {
130: 		var styleIndex = singletonCounter++;
131: 		styleElement = singletonElement || (singletonElement = createStyleElement(options));
132: 		update = applyToSingletonTag.bind(null, styleElement, styleIndex, false);
133: 		remove = applyToSingletonTag.bind(null, styleElement, styleIndex, true);
134: 	} else if(obj.sourceMap &&
135: 		typeof URL === "function" &&
136: 		typeof URL.createObjectURL === "function" &&
137: 		typeof URL.revokeObjectURL === "function" &&
138: 		typeof Blob === "function" &&
139: 		typeof btoa === "function") {
140: 		styleElement = createLinkElement(options);
141: 		update = updateLink.bind(null, styleElement);
142: 		remove = function() {
143: 			removeStyleElement(styleElement);
144: 			if(styleElement.href)
145: 				URL.revokeObjectURL(styleElement.href);
146: 		};
147: 	} else {
148: 		styleElement = createStyleElement(options);
149: 		update = applyToTag.bind(null, styleElement);
150: 		remove = function() {
151: 			removeStyleElement(styleElement);
152: 		};
153: 	}
154: 	update(obj);
155: 	return function updateStyle(newObj) {
156: 		if(newObj) {
157: 			if(newObj.css === obj.css && newObj.media === obj.media && newObj.sourceMap === obj.sourceMap)
158: 				return;
159: 			update(obj = newObj);
160: 		} else {
161: 			remove();
162: 		}
163: 	};
164: }
165: var replaceText = (function () {
166: 	var textStore = [];
167: 	return function (index, replacement) {
168: 		textStore[index] = replacement;
169: 		return textStore.filter(Boolean).join('\n');
170: 	};
171: })();
172: function applyToSingletonTag(styleElement, index, remove, obj) {
173: 	var css = remove ? "" : obj.css;
174: 	if (styleElement.styleSheet) {
175: 		styleElement.styleSheet.cssText = replaceText(index, css);
176: 	} else {
177: 		var cssNode = document.createTextNode(css);
178: 		var childNodes = styleElement.childNodes;
179: 		if (childNodes[index]) styleElement.removeChild(childNodes[index]);
180: 		if (childNodes.length) {
181: 			styleElement.insertBefore(cssNode, childNodes[index]);
182: 		} else {
183: 			styleElement.appendChild(cssNode);
184: 		}
185: 	}
186: }
187: function applyToTag(styleElement, obj) {
188: 	var css = obj.css;
189: 	var media = obj.media;
190: 	if(media) {
191: 		styleElement.setAttribute("media", media)
192: 	}
193: 	if(styleElement.styleSheet) {
194: 		styleElement.styleSheet.cssText = css;
195: 	} else {
196: 		while(styleElement.firstChild) {
197: 			styleElement.removeChild(styleElement.firstChild);
198: 		}
199: 		styleElement.appendChild(document.createTextNode(css));
200: 	}
201: }
202: function updateLink(linkElement, obj) {
203: 	var css = obj.css;
204: 	var sourceMap = obj.sourceMap;
205: 	if(sourceMap) {
206: 		css += "\n/*# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64," + btoa(unescape(encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(sourceMap)))) + " */";
207: 	}
208: 	var blob = new Blob([css], { type: "text/css" });
209: 	var oldSrc = linkElement.href;
210: 	linkElement.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
211: 	if(oldSrc)
212: 		URL.revokeObjectURL(oldSrc);
213: }

  1: #!/bin/sh
  2: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3: # Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one
  4: # or more contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file
  5: # distributed with this work for additional information
  6: # regarding copyright ownership.  The ASF licenses this file
  7: # to you under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the
  8: # "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance
  9: # with the License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
 10: #
 11: #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
 12: #
 13: # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
 14: # software distributed under the License is distributed on an
 15: # "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY
 16: # KIND, either express or implied.  See the License for the
 17: # specific language governing permissions and limitations
 18: # under the License.
 19: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 20: 
 21: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 22: # Maven2 Start Up Batch script
 23: #
 24: # Required ENV vars:
 25: # ------------------
 26: #   JAVA_HOME - location of a JDK home dir
 27: #
 28: # Optional ENV vars
 29: # -----------------
 30: #   M2_HOME - location of maven2's installed home dir
 31: #   MAVEN_OPTS - parameters passed to the Java VM when running Maven
 32: #     e.g. to debug Maven itself, use
 33: #       set MAVEN_OPTS=-Xdebug -Xrunjdwp:transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=8000
 34: #   MAVEN_SKIP_RC - flag to disable loading of mavenrc files
 35: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 36: 
 37: if [ -z "$MAVEN_SKIP_RC" ] ; then
 38: 
 39:   if [ -f /etc/mavenrc ] ; then
 40:     . /etc/mavenrc
 41:   fi
 42: 
 43:   if [ -f "$HOME/.mavenrc" ] ; then
 44:     . "$HOME/.mavenrc"
 45:   fi
 46: 
 47: fi
 48: 
 49: # OS specific support.  $var _must_ be set to either true or false.
 50: cygwin=false;
 51: darwin=false;
 52: mingw=false
 53: case "`uname`" in
 54:   CYGWIN*) cygwin=true ;;
 55:   MINGW*) mingw=true;;
 56:   Darwin*) darwin=true
 57:            #
 58:            # Look for the Apple JDKs first to preserve the existing behaviour, and then look
 59:            # for the new JDKs provided by Oracle.
 60:            #
 61:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L /System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/CurrentJDK ] ; then
 62:              #
 63:              # Apple JDKs
 64:              #
 65:              export JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Frameworks/JavaVM.framework/Versions/CurrentJDK/Home
 66:            fi
 67: 
 68:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L /System/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK ] ; then
 69:              #
 70:              # Apple JDKs
 71:              #
 72:              export JAVA_HOME=/System/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK/Contents/Home
 73:            fi
 74: 
 75:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -L "/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK" ] ; then
 76:              #
 77:              # Oracle JDKs
 78:              #
 79:              export JAVA_HOME=/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/CurrentJDK/Contents/Home
 80:            fi
 81: 
 82:            if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] && [ -x "/usr/libexec/java_home" ]; then
 83:              #
 84:              # Apple JDKs
 85:              #
 86:              export JAVA_HOME=`/usr/libexec/java_home`
 87:            fi
 88:            ;;
 89: esac
 90: 
 91: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
 92:   if [ -r /etc/gentoo-release ] ; then
 93:     JAVA_HOME=`java-config --jre-home`
 94:   fi
 95: fi
 96: 
 97: if [ -z "$M2_HOME" ] ; then
 98:   ## resolve links - $0 may be a link to maven's home
 99:   PRG="$0"
100: 
101:   # need this for relative symlinks
102:   while [ -h "$PRG" ] ; do
103:     ls=`ls -ld "$PRG"`
104:     link=`expr "$ls" : '.*-> \(.*\)$'`
105:     if expr "$link" : '/.*' > /dev/null; then
106:       PRG="$link"
107:     else
108:       PRG="`dirname "$PRG"`/$link"
109:     fi
110:   done
111: 
112:   saveddir=`pwd`
113: 
114:   M2_HOME=`dirname "$PRG"`/..
115: 
116:   # make it fully qualified
117:   M2_HOME=`cd "$M2_HOME" && pwd`
118: 
119:   cd "$saveddir"
120:   # echo Using m2 at $M2_HOME
121: fi
122: 
123: # For Cygwin, ensure paths are in UNIX format before anything is touched
124: if $cygwin ; then
125:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
126:     M2_HOME=`cygpath --unix "$M2_HOME"`
127:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
128:     JAVA_HOME=`cygpath --unix "$JAVA_HOME"`
129:   [ -n "$CLASSPATH" ] &&
130:     CLASSPATH=`cygpath --path --unix "$CLASSPATH"`
131: fi
132: 
133: # For Migwn, ensure paths are in UNIX format before anything is touched
134: if $mingw ; then
135:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
136:     M2_HOME="`(cd "$M2_HOME"; pwd)`"
137:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
138:     JAVA_HOME="`(cd "$JAVA_HOME"; pwd)`"
139:   # TODO classpath?
140: fi
141: 
142: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ]; then
143:   javaExecutable="`which javac`"
144:   if [ -n "$javaExecutable" ] && ! [ "`expr \"$javaExecutable\" : '\([^ ]*\)'`" = "no" ]; then
145:     # readlink(1) is not available as standard on Solaris 10.
146:     readLink=`which readlink`
147:     if [ ! `expr "$readLink" : '\([^ ]*\)'` = "no" ]; then
148:       if $darwin ; then
149:         javaHome="`dirname \"$javaExecutable\"`"
150:         javaExecutable="`cd \"$javaHome\" && pwd -P`/javac"
151:       else
152:         javaExecutable="`readlink -f \"$javaExecutable\"`"
153:       fi
154:       javaHome="`dirname \"$javaExecutable\"`"
155:       javaHome=`expr "$javaHome" : '\(.*\)/bin'`
156:       JAVA_HOME="$javaHome"
157:       export JAVA_HOME
158:     fi
159:   fi
160: fi
161: 
162: if [ -z "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
163:   if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME"  ] ; then
164:     if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
165:       # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
166:       JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java"
167:     else
168:       JAVACMD="$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"
169:     fi
170:   else
171:     JAVACMD="`which java`"
172:   fi
173: fi
174: 
175: if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
176:   echo "Error: JAVA_HOME is not defined correctly." >&2
177:   echo "  We cannot execute $JAVACMD" >&2
178:   exit 1
179: fi
180: 
181: if [ -z "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
182:   echo "Warning: JAVA_HOME environment variable is not set."
183: fi
184: 
185: CLASSWORLDS_LAUNCHER=org.codehaus.plexus.classworlds.launcher.Launcher
186: 
187: # For Cygwin, switch paths to Windows format before running java
188: if $cygwin; then
189:   [ -n "$M2_HOME" ] &&
190:     M2_HOME=`cygpath --path --windows "$M2_HOME"`
191:   [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] &&
192:     JAVA_HOME=`cygpath --path --windows "$JAVA_HOME"`
193:   [ -n "$CLASSPATH" ] &&
194:     CLASSPATH=`cygpath --path --windows "$CLASSPATH"`
195: fi
196: 
197: # traverses directory structure from process work directory to filesystem root
198: # first directory with .mvn subdirectory is considered project base directory
199: find_maven_basedir() {
200:   local basedir=$(pwd)
201:   local wdir=$(pwd)
202:   while [ "$wdir" != '/' ] ; do
203:     if [ -d "$wdir"/.mvn ] ; then
204:       basedir=$wdir
205:       break
206:     fi
207:     wdir=$(cd "$wdir/.."; pwd)
208:   done
209:   echo "${basedir}"
210: }
211: 
212: # concatenates all lines of a file
213: concat_lines() {
214:   if [ -f "$1" ]; then
215:     echo "$(tr -s '\n' ' ' < "$1")"
216:   fi
217: }
218: 
219: export MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=${MAVEN_BASEDIR:-$(find_maven_basedir)}
220: MAVEN_OPTS="$(concat_lines "$MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR/.mvn/jvm.config") $MAVEN_OPTS"
221: 
222: # Provide a "standardized" way to retrieve the CLI args that will
223: # work with both Windows and non-Windows executions.
224: MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS="$MAVEN_CONFIG $@"
225: export MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS
226: 
227: WRAPPER_LAUNCHER=org.apache.maven.wrapper.MavenWrapperMain
228: 
229: exec "$JAVACMD" \
230:   $MAVEN_OPTS \
231:   -classpath "$MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar" \
232:   "-Dmaven.home=${M2_HOME}" "-Dmaven.multiModuleProjectDirectory=${MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR}" \
233:   ${WRAPPER_LAUNCHER} "$@"

 18: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

 20: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 21: @REM Maven2 Start Up Batch script
 22: @REM
 23: @REM Required ENV vars:
 24: @REM JAVA_HOME - location of a JDK home dir
 25: @REM
 26: @REM Optional ENV vars
 27: @REM M2_HOME - location of maven2's installed home dir
 28: @REM MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO - set to 'on' to enable the echoing of the batch commands
 29: @REM MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE - set to 'on' to wait for a key stroke before ending
 30: @REM MAVEN_OPTS - parameters passed to the Java VM when running Maven
 31: @REM     e.g. to debug Maven itself, use
 32: @REM set MAVEN_OPTS=-Xdebug -Xrunjdwp:transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=8000
 33: @REM MAVEN_SKIP_RC - flag to disable loading of mavenrc files
 34: @REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
 35: 
 36: @REM Begin all REM lines with '@' in case MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO is 'on'
 37: @echo off
 38: @REM enable echoing my setting MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO to 'on'
 39: @if "%MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO%" == "on"  echo %MAVEN_BATCH_ECHO%
 40: 
 41: @REM set %HOME% to equivalent of $HOME
 42: if "%HOME%" == "" (set "HOME=%HOMEDRIVE%%HOMEPATH%")
 43: 
 44: @REM Execute a user defined script before this one
 45: if not "%MAVEN_SKIP_RC%" == "" goto skipRcPre
 46: @REM check for pre script, once with legacy .bat ending and once with .cmd ending
 47: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.bat" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.bat"
 48: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.cmd" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_pre.cmd"
 49: :skipRcPre
 50: 
 51: @setlocal
 52: 
 53: set ERROR_CODE=0
 54: 
 55: @REM To isolate internal variables from possible post scripts, we use another setlocal
 56: @setlocal
 57: 
 58: @REM ==== START VALIDATION ====
 59: if not "%JAVA_HOME%" == "" goto OkJHome
 60: 
 61: echo.
 62: echo Error: JAVA_HOME not found in your environment. >&2
 63: echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the >&2
 64: echo location of your Java installation. >&2
 65: echo.
 66: goto error
 67: 
 68: :OkJHome
 69: if exist "%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe" goto init
 70: 
 71: echo.
 72: echo Error: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory. >&2
 73: echo JAVA_HOME = "%JAVA_HOME%" >&2
 74: echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the >&2
 75: echo location of your Java installation. >&2
 76: echo.
 77: goto error
 78: 
 79: @REM ==== END VALIDATION ====
 80: 
 81: :init
 82: 
 83: set MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS=%*
 84: 
 85: @REM Find the project base dir, i.e. the directory that contains the folder ".mvn".
 86: @REM Fallback to current working directory if not found.
 87: 
 88: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%MAVEN_BASEDIR%
 89: IF NOT "%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%"=="" goto endDetectBaseDir
 90: 
 91: set EXEC_DIR=%CD%
 92: set WDIR=%EXEC_DIR%
 93: :findBaseDir
 94: IF EXIST "%WDIR%"\.mvn goto baseDirFound
 95: cd ..
 96: IF "%WDIR%"=="%CD%" goto baseDirNotFound
 97: set WDIR=%CD%
 98: goto findBaseDir
 99: 
100: :baseDirFound
101: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%WDIR%
102: cd "%EXEC_DIR%"
103: goto endDetectBaseDir
104: 
105: :baseDirNotFound
106: set MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR=%EXEC_DIR%
107: cd "%EXEC_DIR%"
108: 
109: :endDetectBaseDir
110: 
111: IF NOT EXIST "%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%\.mvn\jvm.config" goto endReadAdditionalConfig
112: 
113: @setlocal EnableExtensions EnableDelayedExpansion
114: for /F "usebackq delims=" %%a in ("%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%\.mvn\jvm.config") do set JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS=!JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS! %%a
115: @endlocal & set JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS=%JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS%
116: 
117: :endReadAdditionalConfig
118: 
119: SET MAVEN_JAVA_EXE="%JAVA_HOME%\bin\java.exe"
120: 
121: set WRAPPER_JAR="".\.mvn\wrapper\maven-wrapper.jar""
122: set WRAPPER_LAUNCHER=org.apache.maven.wrapper.MavenWrapperMain
123: 
124: %MAVEN_JAVA_EXE% %JVM_CONFIG_MAVEN_PROPS% %MAVEN_OPTS% %MAVEN_DEBUG_OPTS% -classpath %WRAPPER_JAR% "-Dmaven.multiModuleProjectDirectory=%MAVEN_PROJECTBASEDIR%" %WRAPPER_LAUNCHER% %MAVEN_CMD_LINE_ARGS%
125: if ERRORLEVEL 1 goto error
126: goto end
127: 
128: :error
129: set ERROR_CODE=1
130: 
131: :end
132: @endlocal & set ERROR_CODE=%ERROR_CODE%
133: 
134: if not "%MAVEN_SKIP_RC%" == "" goto skipRcPost
135: @REM check for post script, once with legacy .bat ending and once with .cmd ending
136: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.bat" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.bat"
137: if exist "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.cmd" call "%HOME%\mavenrc_post.cmd"
138: :skipRcPost
139: 
140: @REM pause the script if MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE is set to 'on'
141: if "%MAVEN_BATCH_PAUSE%" == "on" pause
142: 
143: if "%MAVEN_TERMINATE_CMD%" == "on" exit %ERROR_CODE%
144: 
145: exit /B %ERROR_CODE%
